useCases.title: Control the player tank
useCases.outcome: The tank moves and its barrel aims within the side-view arena.

attention.question: Should aiming use fixed angle steps or move continuously while an aim key is held?
attention.whyItMatters: This determines input handling, barrel feedback, and how precisely the player can line up a shot.

alternatives.implication: Each key press changes the barrel by a fixed angle for predictable keyboard control.
Holding an aim key rotates the barrel smoothly for finer control.

steps.userAction: Hold the left or right movement key.
steps.systemResponse: The player tank moves horizontally while remaining inside the arena bounds.

steps.userAction: Use the aim-up or aim-down key.
steps.systemResponse: The barrel angle changes according to the selected aiming model and remains within its limits.

useCases.title: Fire at the enemy tank
useCases.outcome: The shot hits the enemy for a win or leaves the arena for a loss.

steps.userAction: Press the fire key while the round is active.
steps.systemResponse: The game launches one visible projectile from the barrel using the current tank position and aim.
The game advances the shot; hitting the enemy wins, while leaving the arena loses.

useCases.title: Finish and restart a round
useCases.outcome: The player sees a clear win or loss and can start a fresh round.

steps.userAction: Hit the enemy or let the fired shot leave the arena.
steps.systemResponse: The game stops accepting play controls and prominently displays Win or Lose.

steps.userAction: Press the restart control after the round ends.
steps.systemResponse: The game restores initial tank, enemy, projectile, and round state without reloading or saving data.

contract.title: Tank target-practice runtime contract
contract.context: A local single-page keyboard game with one player tank, one enemy target, transient runtime state, and no network or persistence.

participants.name: Player
participants.responsibility: Provides keyboard commands and chooses when to restart.

participants.name: Game page
participants.responsibility: Captures input and presents the arena, controls, projectile, and round outcome.

participants.name: Game engine
participants.responsibility: Updates movement, aiming, projectile physics, collisions, and round state.

input.name: Movement command
input.description: Left or right direction plus current key state.

guarantees.statement: The player tank never moves outside the playable arena.

input.name: Aim command
input.description: Aim-up or aim-down input interpreted using the selected aim model.

output.name: Barrel angle
output.description: The updated angle clamped to the allowed firing arc.

guarantees.statement: The barrel angle remains inside the visible, playable firing arc.

input.name: Fire command
input.description: A fire request using the current player position and barrel angle.

output.name: Projectile state
output.description: A visible active projectile launched from the barrel muzzle.

errors.meaning: A shot cannot be fired after a win or loss.
A new shot cannot be fired while the current projectile is active.

guarantees.statement: At most one player projectile is active at a time.
Every projectile begins at the current barrel muzzle.

input.name: Elapsed frame time
input.description: Time elapsed since the previous animation update.

output.name: Frame state
output.description: Updated projectile, collision, enemy, and round outcome state.

guarantees.statement: Enemy contact produces Win; exiting the arena produces Lose.
Movement, aiming, and firing stop when the round is terminal.

input.name: Restart command
input.description: A restart request issued after a terminal outcome.

output.name: Initial round state
output.description: Fresh player, enemy, projectile, and active-round state.

errors.meaning: Restart is unavailable while the current round is active.

guarantees.statement: Restart creates the same playable initial state without retaining prior-round data.

storageContracts.name: Ephemeral game state
storageContracts.purpose: Hold only the current frame and round state while the page is open.

records.name: Round state
records.description: Current entities, projectile, and outcome for one local round.

fields.name: barrelAngle
fields.description: Current barrel angle within the allowed arc.

fields.name: enemyPosition
fields.description: Fixed enemy target position for the round.

fields.name: projectile
fields.description: Current shot state or null when no shot is active.

constraints.statement: Exactly one enemy target exists in each round.
Runtime state is never written to browser storage or sent over a network.

guarantees.statement: Closing or reloading the page discards all game state.

lifecycleRules.statement: Create initial round state when the page loads.
Replace the entire round state when restart is invoked.
Discard state when the page context ends.
A round remains active until the shot hits the enemy or exits the arena.
A Win or Lose state remains visible and inert until restart.

controlFlows.title: Play, resolve, and restart a round
controlFlows.purpose: Describe the complete local gameplay loop and its terminal outcomes.

guiSketches.title: Side-view target-practice page
guiSketches.purpose: Keep the compact game, keyboard help, status, and restart action visible on one page.

elements.label: Round status: Active, Win, or Lose

layers.name: Single game page
layers.responsibility: Render the side-view arena, instructions, entities, status, and restart action.

technologies.name: Existing page stack
technologies.role: Use the repository's current UI and styling tooling unchanged.

layers.name: In-page game loop
layers.responsibility: Process keyboard state, update entities, resolve collisions, and manage outcomes.

technologies.name: Browser animation APIs
technologies.role: Drive local frame updates and projectile motion.

layers.name: Ephemeral memory state
layers.responsibility: Hold one current round without networking or persistence.

technologies.name: In-memory objects
technologies.role: Store runtime-only entity and outcome state.

conclusion.goal: Deliver a tiny, understandable side-view tank target-practice loop on one local page.
conclusion.summary: The design covers keyboard movement, an explicitly unresolved aiming model, one shot per round, one enemy, terminal Win or Lose feedback, and clean restart using only ephemeral in-page state.

aspects.title: Bounded local gameplay
aspects.summary: Commands are accepted only during active play, with one projectile and one enemy per round.

aspects.title: Complete round loop
aspects.summary: Control leads to firing and simulation, then a terminal outcome and restart.

aspects.title: No external services
aspects.summary: Rendering, simulation, and transient state remain in the existing browser stack.

aspects.title: Single-page arena
aspects.summary: The arena, keyboard help, outcome, and restart affordance remain visible and focused.

notes: A shot that hits the enemy wins; a shot that leaves any arena edge loses.
No networking, browser storage, saved progress, or tooling modification is part of this design.

reviewSummary.headline: A complete local tank-practice loop is designed with one aiming choice left to the player.

changes.title: Define the playable round
changes.description: Added movement, aiming, one-shot firing, projectile resolution, Win or Lose, and restart.
changes.whyItMatters: This turns the small concept into a bounded, implementable gameplay loop.

changes.title: Keep all state local and temporary
changes.description: Specified an in-memory round model with no network or persistent storage.
changes.whyItMatters: This directly preserves the requested standalone scope and privacy boundary.

changes.title: Leave aiming behavior open
changes.description: Marked stepped versus continuous keyboard aiming as a blocking product choice.
changes.whyItMatters: The chosen feel affects input processing and player precision.

changes.title: Focus the page layout
changes.description: Placed the arena, status, controls help, and restart affordance in one compact view.
changes.whyItMatters: Players can understand and replay the game without navigation or setup.
